results.note: Matches 2.1 Procedure (PDF p. 3) and the p. 3 part of Introduction paragraph 3. 'Participating federal, state, local and tribal agencies' joins two adjacent sentences fairly.
All counts, β/SE/p and percentages checked on rendered pp. 1-3, 6 and recomputed; 68/492 and 635/2,174 correct. My Fig. 1 pixel readings show the share equals pill/(pill+powder) in every quarter.

My 300-dpi pixel readings: powder peak about 2,058 (2021 Q3; 'about 2,060' fits better), pill seizures about 675 (Q3), pills about 2.73 million and powder about 2,919 kg (Q2); shares 0.215, 0.173; 0.292 highest.
Discussion paragraph 4 (p. 4) and 4.1 Limitations (pp. 5-6) match. The authors then call it 'more than plausible' that seizures reflect greater overall availability; not needed here.

Methods (p. 949, continuing atop p. 950) and footnotes §, ¶, ** match: four states, Louisiana added in 2021; flagging, two-coauthor coding and the five criteria are accurate. Per-criterion and tested-pill counts are indeed absent.
Abstract, Results paragraph 1 and Figure (footnote † lists the eight western jurisdictions) match; 'driven by' is the report's own wording. No tests, intervals or quarterly numerators printed.
My 300-dpi trace against the axis ticks: total 2.33, 3.82, 4.23, 5.12, 4.92, 4.73; West 13.2, 14.0, 13.4, then 14.7 (its highest). Discussion paragraph 1 (p. 954) says below 6% and more than doubled.
Table 1 (p. 951) and footnotes ¶, **, †† (p. 952) match; all percentages recompute from the counts (2,437/54,768 = 4.4%; 1,009/2,437 = 41.4%; 10,226/52,331 = 19.5%).
Discussion paragraph 3 (the sentence is on p. 954; the paragraph runs onto p. 955) keeps the report's hedge ('suggests ... likely'); Limitations (p. 955) match.

Methods paragraphs 3-4 (PDF pp. 6-7), Results paragraphs 1 (p. 7) and 6 (p. 9) and Discussion (p. 10) match; 'two SCS' is also in Results paragraph 1. No pill counts, and Figures 1-2 give results by expected drug only, not by form.

key_findings.note: My readings (300 dpi, pixel measurement): powder-seizure peak about 2,058 (about 2,060 rather than 2,050); pills seized about 1.77 million (2020 Q3) and about 0.89 million (2020 Q4); fitted share at 2021 Q4 about 0.27. All within reading error.
The authors also cite rising illicit production, perceived abundance and ease of transport (DEA), and hedge the conclusion as 'more than plausible'.

reporting_issues.note: My trace of the Fig. 2 right fitted curve: quarter-to-quarter rises grow from about 0.11 to about 0.25 million, then shrink to about 0.21 million, so it is clearly curved.
My readings at 2018 Q1: fitted line about -0.10 million, band lower edge about -0.59 million; powder-weight band about -43 kg; pill-seizure band about -13.
Fig. 1 caption and axis also say 'out of all fentanyl seizures' / 'of Total Seizures'; my quarterly readings fit pill/(pill+powder) in all 16 quarters.

risk_of_bias.note: Design (registry), JBI prevalence checklist and overall moderate (high as a supply indicator) agreed.

interpretation_gap.note: Minor: the counterfeit-pill risk conclusion rests on cited literature, as the card says.

missed: Discussion paragraph 3 (PDF p. 4) says the results corroborate a study finding no COVID-19 dip and that fentanyl availability 'increased consistently', but Figs 1-2 show quarterly falls (powder seizures about 1,071 to 950, 2020 Q1-Q2, and about 1,436 to 1,224, 2020 Q3-Q4; pills seized about 1.77 to 0.89 million, 2020 Q3-Q4): stated more strongly than the quarterly data.

risk_of_bias.note: Registry design, JBI prevalence and overall moderate agreed. But the reasoning's 'rarely rests on tested pills' (and cannot_establish's 'not tested in most cases') is not stated in the report, which gives no count of tested pills: write 'the number resting on tested pills is not reported'.

interpretation_gap.note: Minor; the causal and market readings are hedged and the card flags them.

missed: cannot_establish says pill contents 'were not tested in most cases' and the RoB reasoning says the evidence 'rarely rests on tested pills'; the report gives no such figure (criterion 2 shows that some pills were tested). Reword as 'the number of deaths with tested pills is not reported'.
Discussion paragraph 3 (pp. 954-955) also reads the xylazine difference as suggesting different IMF sources for pills and powders: a speculative inference from one adulterant percentage, not flagged.

key_findings.note: Data tables read on the rendered pages; each category sums to its printed total (907, 99, 141, 256, 140, 143).

reporting_issues.note: 182 days at 4 site-shifts a week is about 104 shifts, about 16.5 checks per shift. If 'two days a week' meant both sites together (about 52 shifts), it would be about 33. Either way 24 does not reconcile without the shift count.

risk_of_bias.note: Cross-sectional, JBI prevalence, overall high (as a market estimate) agreed. My recomputed Wilson intervals match all of the card's intervals.

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial: an unhedged market-wide reading in the Discussion from samples the Results call unrepresentative, 'significantly higher' uptake without a test, and a public-health potential with no outcome data.
